chapter: Chicago, Virginia Ravens and the northern territory bands
title: Rejoining the Virginia Ravens and bringing in the Thomas brothers
summary: At Milwaukee's Metropole the Ravens' bus gave him back his job. He brought in LeRoy White, Joe Thomas and Merle Williams, and pianist Frank Hines began telling him he did not know his chords.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: And while I was in Milwaukee, one day I was walking down to the place called the Metropole there, where the musicians hung out. And I walked down there and there was the Virginia Ravens' bus. So I walked over and the guys was glad to see me and they gave me my job back. So I went on back with them and I stayed -- we played around there with them all -- somewhere up in Wisconsin, Eau Claire and Black River Falls and all that. And finally they needed a trumpet player. Well, I found this boy, Leroy White, he was down in Pittsburgh, Kansas playing with Walter Thomas and a bunch of them,

Jameson's band down in Wichita. And I got him and Joe Thomas, who was Walter Thomas' brother, to come up from there to play with the Virginia Ravens. And then also Merle Williams was home, he came back with the Virginia Ravens.
Now, this is Joe Thomas the tenor player?
Not the one with Jimmy Lunceford. He was an alto player, Joe Thomas. He's here in New York now. He's a writer, he's with --

Joe Thomas was the alto player but he was Walter Foots Thomas' brother. And they had all been together down in Wichita. So they came and joined the Virginia Ravens. And then Merle left and a piano player out of Springfield, Missouri, I think that's right -- now, Springfield, Illinois, named Frank Hines. He took put Merle's place. And Frank was a marvelous piano player, he played something like Earl Hines. So we were with the Virginians and Frank used to say to me, "Eddie, you play a great jazz saxophone. But, he said, you don't know your chords." So I said chords, what do you mean?" So he started telling me about the C7, B flat 7, F7. So he says, I'm going to buy you a record.
